newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber up on short covering, spread unwinding.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber up on short covering, spread unwinding.

text.p: Light short covering and unwinding of bear spreads kept CME lumber futures mostly higher at the close, traders said.
Lumber closed $6.70 per tbf higher to $0.60 lower with March up most at $413.20 and May up $1.60 at $385.80 per tbf. Only September posted a loss.
Futures ran up early as carryover selling was lacking. The market held technical support and moved higher as short covering developed, traders said.
However, fundamentals remained on the negative side which pressured prices at times. Cash trade was quiet, they said.
Prudential Securities, Lind-Waldock and Saul Stone bought while ING and Rosenthal Collins sold, pit sources added.
